subproblem.title: An n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P is the span of an orthonormal n-frame
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with dim V = n. Then there is an orthonormal family v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, indexed by Fin n, with span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the selected proof ("As dim V = n, V has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank ℝ V = n); let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be its image in ℝ^P. Then v is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span{v_0, …, v_d} = V"), stated for an arbitrary dimension n.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; V carries the restricted inner product and is a finite-dimensional real inner product space; ι := V.subtype : V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ^P is the inclusion, which is the linear isometry V.subtypeₗᵢ.
1. (An orthonormal basis of V indexed by Fin n.) A finite-dimensional real inner product space has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin (finrank): stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (finrank ℝ V)) ℝ V. Reindexing it along the bijection finCongr h : Fin (finrank ℝ V) ≃ Fin n given by the hypothesis h : finrank ℝ V = n (OrthonormalBasis.reindex) yields an orthonormal basis b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) of V.
2. (Orthonormal in ℝ^P.) Put v_i := ι(b_i) = ↑b_i ∈ ℝ^P. A linear isometry preserves inner products, so ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = ⟨b_i, b_j⟩ = [i = j]; that is, v is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry applied to b.orthonormal and V.subtypeₗᵢ).
3. (Span.) range v = ι(range b) (Set.range_comp), so span(range v) = map ι (span(range b)) (Submodule.span_image). The vectors of a basis span the whole space, span(range b) = ⊤ (Basis.span_eq for b.toBasis, whose underlying family is b by OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis). Hence span(range v) = map ι ⊤ = range ι = V (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
4. (Conclusion.) v : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal and span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V. (For n = 0, V = 0 and v is the empty family; the argument is uniform in n.) ∎

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_exists_orthonormal_frame_of_finrank_eq : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V := by
  intro P n V hV
  let b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) ℝ V := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V).reindex (finCongr hV)
  refine ⟨fun i => (b i : Euclid P), ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact b.orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry V.subtypeₗᵢ
  · have hrange : Set.range (fun i => (b i : Euclid P)) = (V.subtype) '' Set.range b := by
      rw [← Set.range_comp]; rfl
    have hb : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range b) = ⊤ := by
      simpa [OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis] using b.toBasis.span_eq
    rw [hrange, Submodule.span_image, hb, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype]
proof_key_steps: Reindex stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V along finrank ℝ V = n to an orthonormal basis b of V indexed by Fin n.
v_i := ↑b_i is orthonormal in ℝ^P because the inclusion V.subtypeₗᵢ is a linear isometry.
span(range v) = map V.subtype (span(range b)) = map V.subtype ⊤ = V.
